The accusative σε is among the most common forms in New Testament Greek. Ancient Greek carefully distinguished singular from plural second person pronouns (unlike modern English), making the singular forms crucial for indicating direct personal address to an individual rather than a group. These pronouns carried significant weight in prayer, commandments, and personal confrontation."
